title: 对于英伟达来说，谷歌的人工智能芯片业务正变得越来越难以忽视
content:
Earlier this year, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang downplayed the threat of other companies building competing AI chips, including Google.
"Without Anthropic, why would there be any TPU growth at all?" he said in an interview with podcaster Dwarkesh Patel, referring to Google's custom chips. "It's 100% Anthropic."
That is no longer the case.
On Tuesday, Google and Oracle announced a blockbuster deal that will see Google's TPUs, short for Tensor Processing Units, made available to Oracle cloud customers from next year. As the companies underscored in a joint announcement, it's the first time Google's TPUs have been offered on a hyperscaler's platform beyond its own.
Anthropic isn't the only one Nvidia should be worried about. OpenAI has a job listing for a software engineer to optimize its models for TPUs, and The Information reported Tuesday that OpenAI plans to buy TPUs from Google.
Meanwhile, several analysts have predicted Google's TPU business is about to explode as more companies hedge their bets with a multichip strategy — providing an opening for Google and others to further move onto Nvidia's turf.
Despite this, Nvidia's chip business still eclipses everyone else's, including Google, which is also a big customer of Nvidia's GPUs. Yet Google's AI chips, which the company began building more than a decade ago to power search and other products, might be poised for takeoff.
On Wednesday, during Google's third-quarter earnings call, chief financial officer Anat Ashkenazi said the company expects a "meaningful revenue ramp in 2027" in TPU sales.
Cloud chief Thomas Kurian also said on the call that TPU sales were a "meaningful contributor" to the company's Q3 financials.
In its IPO paperwork filed this week, Anthropic said it planned to spend $114.5 billion on Google compute between April 2026 and July 2033. While it didn't specify how much of that would go to TPUs specifically, it estimated spending between $125 billion and $150 billion on TPU capacity from Google and other providers.
In the same filing, Anthropic said it's also using Amazon's Trainium chips and AMD's GPUs, as well as chips from Nvidia and Google.
All told, this might be Nvidia's nightmare scenario coming true. If companies are increasingly using a multichip strategy, it could hamper Nvidia's pricing power.
Google declined to comment, and Nvidia and OpenAI did not respond to requests for comment.
TPU takeoff?
Google's TPU business may only be getting started.
In notes published this month, Japanese banking group Mizuho projected TPU revenue of $28 billion for 2026 and $67 billion in 2027. Mizuho said Google could see that number reach as high as $100 billion in 2028, while TD Cowen's John Blackledge projected it could reach $138 billion, accounting for 34% of Google Cloud's 2028 revenue.
That number is still dwarfed by Nvidia, which reported $96.2 billion in revenue in the previous quarter alone, and the market reacted with a shrug on Wednesday as its share price stayed flat.
Some analysts, though, think the market is underestimating Google, especially as more companies look to reduce their reliance on Nvidia's GPUs.
"We believe Google's TPU hardware business is emerging as a materially larger opportunity than what is currently reflected in consensus estimates," Mizuho analysts wrote in a note published October 18, adding that selling TPUs outright — rather than renting them from Google's own data centers — could ease Google's aggressive capex spending.
And even if that spending continues to soar — and right now, there are no signs the foot is coming off the accelerator — analysts at Bank of America said Google's cash-splashing looks "relatively efficient" compared to its peers, as TPUs continue to power the company's own AI efforts.
For Google, it's the payoff of a decade-plus investment in silicon that was originally designed to make Search smarter. It could also act as something of a buffer against damage to its core search business as AI agents eat Google's lunch, Mizuho also said this month.

report.summary: 谷歌TPU首次对外供应甲骨文云，英伟达垄断地位承压
report.background: 谷歌自十多年前开始自研TPU，最初只为支撑搜索等自家产品，长期仅供内部及少数客户使用。英伟达CEO黄仁勋今年初还曾公开淡化TPU威胁，称其增长几乎全靠Anthropic一家。但局面在近期急转：谷歌与甲骨文达成协议，将于明年向甲骨文云客户开放TPU，这是TPU首次登陆非谷歌的超大规模云平台；同时OpenAI被曝招聘工程师为TPU优化模型、并计划采购TPU。在AI算力需求爆炸、云厂商纷纷寻求多芯片策略以降低对英伟达依赖的大背景下，TPU正从“内部自用”走向“对外销售”的商业化拐点。
key_points: 谷歌与甲骨文达成重磅合作，明年起甲骨文云客户可直接使用谷歌TPU，这是TPU首次在谷歌自家云之外的超大规模平台上提供。
OpenAI开始为TPU优化模型并计划采购，加上Anthropic承诺未来数年投入上千亿美元算力，TPU客户群正从单一大户走向多元化。
分析师普遍看多：Mizuho预计TPU收入2026年280亿美元、2027年670亿美元，2028年或达千亿；TD Cowen更给出138亿美元级别之外的乐观预测。
谷歌CFO在财报电话会上确认，预计2027年TPU销售将迎来“有意义的收入爬坡”，云业务负责人称TPU已是三季度业绩的重要贡献项。
不过英伟达单季营收就达962亿美元，规模仍远超TPU业务，短期格局未变，但多芯片策略可能削弱其定价权。
report.impact: 对AI行业而言，这意味着算力供给从“英伟达一家独大”走向“GPU＋TPU＋Trainium等多芯片并存”，云厂商议价能力增强，硬件价格与供应紧张有望缓解。对开发者来说，模型训练与推理多了一个可选后端，JAX/XLA生态和TPU适配工具的价值上升，但也带来跨芯片移植的额外工程成本。对普通用户，竞争加剧有望压低AI推理成本，让更多AI产品以更低价格、更高并发提供服务，同时谷歌也借此对冲AI搜索对核心广告业务的冲击。
report.tools: 想跟进可关注：Google Cloud TPU（Trillium/Ironwood代际）与JAX、PyTorch/XLA框架；推理侧可看vLLM的TPU后端、SGLang、MaxText等开源项目；关注甲骨文云OCI后续公布的TPU实例规格与定价，以及在多芯片策略下做模型可移植性抽象的工具链。
